message.content: Search for the Linux kernel header file ppdev.h to find all ppdev ioctl definitions. Look in /usr/include/linux/ppdev.h and also try to find it in any kernel source directories. I need the complete list of all ioctl commands defined for ppdev, their ioctl numbers (using _IOR, _IOW, etc. macros), and any structs or flags defined. Also look at /usr/include/linux/parport.h for IEEE1284 mode flags and any related definitions.

    18→#ifndef _LINUX_PPDEV_H
    19→#define _LINUX_PPDEV_H
    20→
    21→#define PP_IOCTL	'p'
    22→
    23→/* Set mode for read/write (e.g. IEEE1284_MODE_EPP) */
    24→#define PPSETMODE	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x80, int)
    25→

    34→struct ppdev_frob_struct {

    42→#define PPWDATA		_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x86, unsigned char)

    49→#define PPRFIFO		OBSOLETE__IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x89, unsigned char)
    50→#define PPWFIFO		OBSOLETE__IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x8a, unsigned char)
    51→
    52→/* Claim the port to start using it */
    53→#define PPCLAIM		_IO(PP_IOCTL, 0x8b)
    54→
    55→/* Release the port when you aren't using it */
    56→#define PPRELEASE	_IO(PP_IOCTL, 0x8c)
    57→
    58→/* Yield the port (release it if another driver is waiting,
    59→ * then reclaim) */
    60→#define PPYIELD		_IO(PP_IOCTL, 0x8d)
    61→
    62→/* Register device exclusively (must be before PPCLAIM). */
    63→#define PPEXCL		_IO(PP_IOCTL, 0x8f)

    66→#define PPDATADIR	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x90, int)

    69→#define PPNEGOT		_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x91, int)

    72→#define PPWCTLONIRQ	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x92, unsigned char)

    74→/* Clear (and return) interrupt count. */
    75→#define PPCLRIRQ	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x93, int)

    78→#define PPSETPHASE	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x94, int)

    81→#define PPGETTIME	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x95, struct timeval)
    82→#define PPSETTIME	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x96, struct timeval)
    83→

    85→#define PPGETMODES	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x97, unsigned int)

    88→#define PPGETMODE	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x98, int)
    89→#define PPGETPHASE	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x99, int)

    92→#define PPGETFLAGS	_IOR(PP_IOCTL, 0x9a, int)
    93→#define PPSETFLAGS	_IOW(PP_IOCTL, 0x9b, int)

    96→#define PP_FASTWRITE	(1<<2)
    97→#define PP_FASTREAD	(1<<3)
    98→#define PP_W91284PIC	(1<<4)

    95→#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_8		(1<<3) /* 8-bit EPP transfers */
    96→

    98→#endif /* _PARPORT_H_ */

Perfect! I've found and extracted all the ppdev ioctl definitions and related headers. Here's a comprehensive summary:

## PPDEV IOCTL Definitions

**Location:** `/usr/include/linux/ppdev.h`

### Master IOCTL Character Code
- **PP_IOCTL** = `'p'` (0x70)

### Complete IOCTL Command List

| Command | Macro Type | Ioctl Number | Data Type | Purpose |
|---------|-----------|--------------|-----------|---------|
| PPSETMODE | _IOW | 0x80 | int | Set mode for read/write (e.g. IEEE1284_MODE_EPP) |
| PPRSTATUS | _IOR | 0x81 | unsigned char | Read status |
| PPWSTATUS | OBSOLETE | 0x82 | unsigned char | (Obsolete - Write status) |
| PPRCONTROL | _IOR | 0x83 | unsigned char | Read control |
| PPWCONTROL | _IOW | 0x84 | unsigned char | Write control |
| PPRDATA | _IOR | 0x85 | unsigned char | Read data |
| PPWDATA | _IOW | 0x86 | unsigned char | Write data |
| PPRECONTROL | OBSOLETE | 0x87 | unsigned char | (Obsolete - Read econtrol) |
| PPWECONTROL | OBSOLETE | 0x88 | unsigned char | (Obsolete - Write econtrol) |
| PPRFIFO | OBSOLETE | 0x89 | unsigned char | (Obsolete - Read FIFO) |
| PPWFIFO | OBSOLETE | 0x8a | unsigned char | (Obsolete - Write FIFO) |
| PPCLAIM | _IO | 0x8b | (none) | Claim the port to start using it |
| PPRELEASE | _IO | 0x8c | (none) | Release the port when not using it |
| PPYIELD | _IO | 0x8d | (none) | Yield the port (release if another driver waiting, then reclaim) |
| PPFCONTROL | _IOW | 0x8e | struct ppdev_frob_struct | Frob control lines |
| PPEXCL | _IO | 0x8f | (none) | Register device exclusively (must be before PPCLAIM) |
| PPDATADIR | _IOW | 0x90 | int | Data line direction (non-zero for input mode) |
| PPNEGOT | _IOW | 0x91 | int | Negotiate a particular IEEE 1284 mode |
| PPWCTLONIRQ | _IOW | 0x92 | unsigned char | Set control lines when an interrupt occurs |
| PPCLRIRQ | _IOR | 0x93 | int | Clear (and return) interrupt count |
| PPSETPHASE | _IOW | 0x94 | int | Set the IEEE 1284 phase (e.g. IEEE1284_PH_FWD_IDLE) |
| PPGETTIME | _IOR | 0x95 | struct timeval | Get port timeout |
| PPSETTIME | _IOW | 0x96 | struct timeval | Set port timeout |
| PPGETMODES | _IOR | 0x97 | unsigned int | Get available modes (what the hardware can do) |
| PPGETMODE | _IOR | 0x98 | int | Get the current mode |
| PPGETPHASE | _IOR | 0x99 | int | Get the current phase |
| PPGETFLAGS | _IOR | 0x9a | int | Get flags |
| PPSETFLAGS | _IOW | 0x9b | int | Set flags |

### Structures

**ppdev_frob_struct** (used with PPFCONTROL):
```c
struct ppdev_frob_struct {
    unsigned char mask;
    unsigned char val;
};
```

### PPDEV Flags (used with PPGETFLAGS/PPSETFLAGS)
- **PP_FASTWRITE** = (1<<2) = 0x04 - Fast write mode
- **PP_FASTREAD** = (1<<3) = 0x08 - Fast read mode
- **PP_W91284PIC** = (1<<4) = 0x10 - Warp9 w91284pic device present
- **PP_FLAGMASK** = (PP_FASTWRITE | PP_FASTREAD | PP_W91284PIC) = 0x1C - Mask for user-visible flags

---

## IEEE1284 Mode Flags (from /usr/include/linux/parport.h)

### IEEE1284 Mode Constants
```c
#define IEEE1284_MODE_NIBBLE             0
#define IEEE1284_MODE_BYTE              (1<<0)      // 0x01
#define IEEE1284_MODE_COMPAT            (1<<8)      // 0x100
#define IEEE1284_MODE_BECP              (1<<9)      // 0x200 (Bounded ECP mode)
#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECP               (1<<4)      // 0x10
#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECPRLE            (IEEE1284_MODE_ECP | (1<<5))  // 0x30 (ECP with RLE)
#define IEEE1284_MODE_ECPSWE            (1<<10)     // 0x400 (Software-emulated)
#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPP               (1<<6)      // 0x40
#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPPSL             (1<<11)     // 0x800 (EPP 1.7)
#define IEEE1284_MODE_EPPSWE            (1<<12)     // 0x1000 (Software-emulated)
#define IEEE1284_DEVICEID               (1<<2)      // 0x04 (Flag)
#define IEEE1284_EXT_LINK               (1<<14)     // 0x4000 (Extensibility link flag)
#define IEEE1284_ADDR                   (1<<13)     // 0x2000 (Address operations flag)
#define IEEE1284_DATA                    0           // Data operations flag
```

### Parport Hardware Modes
```c
#define PARPORT_MODE_PCSPP             (1<<0)  // IBM PC registers available
#define PARPORT_MODE_TRISTATE          (1<<1)  // Can tristate
#define PARPORT_MODE_EPP               (1<<2)  // Hardware EPP
#define PARPORT_MODE_ECP               (1<<3)  // Hardware ECP
#define PARPORT_MODE_COMPAT            (1<<4)  // Hardware 'printer protocol'
#define PARPORT_MODE_DMA               (1<<5)  // Hardware can DMA
#define PARPORT_MODE_SAFEININT         (1<<6)  // SPP registers accessible in IRQ
```

### Parport Control Lines
```c
#define PARPORT_CONTROL_STROBE          0x1
#define PARPORT_CONTROL_AUTOFD          0x2
#define PARPORT_CONTROL_INIT            0x4
#define PARPORT_CONTROL_SELECT          0x8
```

### Parport Status Lines
```c
#define PARPORT_STATUS_ERROR            0x8
#define PARPORT_STATUS_SELECT           0x10
#define PARPORT_STATUS_PAPEROUT         0x20
#define PARPORT_STATUS_ACK              0x40
#define PARPORT_STATUS_BUSY             0x80
```

### Parport EPP Block Transfer Flags
```c
#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST               (1<<0)   // Unreliable counts
#define PARPORT_W91284PIC              (1<<1)   // Have a Warp9 w91284pic in the device
#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_32            PARPORT_EPP_FAST  // 32-bit EPP transfers
#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_16            (1<<2)   // 16-bit EPP transfers
#define PARPORT_EPP_FAST_8             (1<<3)   // 8-bit EPP transfers
```

- **Total PPDEV IOCTLs:** 22 active commands (+ 5 obsolete)
- **IOCTL Range:** 0x80-0x9b
